column1: # This is a SEPARATE channel from cited-paths-exempt.tsv on purpose: a row
# there says "this path is not tracked here and that is fine", which would
# also silence a genuinely dangling path if reused for line checks. A row
# here says "this file's cited line number is known and is not this change's
# problem" -- the path itself still gets the ordinary tier-0 check. Every row
# is scoped to one EXACT citation, never a bare path, because a bare
# exemption would also wave through a future wrong line number for that path.
# THE SWEEP THAT PRODUCED THIS FILE (backlog-226, 2026-07-31): every tracked
# .ml/.mli/.md `path:NNN` citation was enumerated and checked against the
# cited file's current line count. 729 total citations carry a line number or
# range; 39 named a line past the end of the cited file. Of those 39:
#   - 14 (9 distinct file/path pairs, rows below marked AUDIT) sit inside
#     ("Audit date: 2026-05-05. Baseline: <sha>" in its README) that cites
#     line numbers as they stood on that baseline commit, several of them
#     under a heading explicitly marked "(former)". Fixing these to the
#     PRESENT line numbers would corrupt the audit -- the whole point of a
#     dated snapshot is that its citations do NOT track HEAD.
#   - 25 are live, undated documentation whose citations have genuinely
#     drifted (rows below marked DRIFT). These are NOT fixed by this change:
#     several point at content that moved when a backend/module was factored
#     into a thin forwarding `include` (the same class of drift backlog-185
#     exists to fix, one instance of which -- kb/backends/vulkan.md's
#     Sarek_ir_codegen.ml:147 citation -- motivated this very ticket), and
#     mechanically "correcting" a line number without confirming the cited
#     CONTENT is still what the prose describes would risk manufacturing a
#     new wrong citation with high confidence. Precedent for measuring and
#     explicitly carving a backlog out of scope rather than guessing at a fix
#     is backlog-402 (109 portable spellings measured and ruled out of
#     scope). Follow-up: file a backlog item per doc family above to correct
#     these against their current, real locations.
# Shipping tier 1 as a hard gate today, with this backlog unexempted, would
# fail CI on 39 pre-existing citations this change did not introduce -- a
# gate landing red like that is a gate someone disables. Exempting the KNOWN
# backlog and enforcing everything else (including every NEW citation from
# this point on) is the same rollout shape cited-paths-exempt.tsv already
